technical_errors: The block's aggregate-level fields borrow single-failure vocabulary without ever defining how a multi-failure migration report rolls up to one value. `phase` (line 274) and `class` (line 275) are introduced as fields the block "reuses ... from dv-sim-log-first-error" (line 258), where in that sibling skill they describe ONE failure. This migration block can carry many new-only failures, each already classified by step 6's own eight-way local taxonomy (new diagnostic / seed noise until shown otherwise / drop behaviour change / newly exposed / tool semantics change / infrastructure / tool or VIP regression / measurement broken) — none of which is literally the registered token "design". No step says how those per-failure judgments become the block's single top-level `phase` or `class` value, or whether that value describes the whole migration, its worst finding, or something else. This is the same shape of bug as the two confirmed C005 findings on `cov model` and `gate` (a value offered that no step ever tells the reader to assign) and probably escaped the checker only because "infrastructure"/"unknown" happen to appear elsewhere in the body for unrelated reasons, while "identical" and "accept-with-debt" do not.

Step 1 instructs the reader to freeze six things: "RTL revision, testbench revision, filelists, seed set, coverage exclusion files and farm queue" (line 120-121). The block's `frozen` field (line 266) offers only five: "<RTL revision, testbench revision, filelist, seed set, farm queue, or \"not frozen\">" — coverage exclusion files silently drop out between the procedure and the report template, so a reader filling the block from its own field list would never record whether exclusions were frozen, even though step 8's exclusion-drift Gotcha (renamed covergroups leaving exclusions matching nothing) depends on exactly that fact.
verb_honesty: No violations found. Every heavy verb is explicitly handed to the engineer: step 1 ("Ask the engineer to pin both sides to one revision on a branch and confirm which revision that is"), step 4's control rerun ("Ask the engineer to repeat the old version once more over a different seed set of the same size and give you that summary's path"), step 8 ("Ask the engineer to generate each side's report under its own version and give you both paths" plus the explicit "Do not merge across the boundary"), and step 9 ("The agent cannot time anything, so every figure here was either read from a file whose path you were given or reported to you by a person"). The framing sentence's promise ("It cannot start a simulation, merge a coverage database, time anything, or open a vendor portal; every step needing one of those ends in a named handoff") is honored throughout the Procedure.

Borderline, not a hard violation: step 9's "Take the median of at least three repeats per side on the same class of host" has the agent computing a summary statistic. It is defensible as arithmetic over numbers already Read or reported (no tool invocation, no farm job), but it sits close to the line — a stricter phrasing would be "ask the engineer for at least three repeats and the median they report".
hallucination_risks: None found at high confidence. The author routes essentially every team-specific fact (banner strings, marker text, coverage-report shape, farm limits, vendor case process, deprecation switch name) through a [[FILL:]] slot instead of inventing one. The one borderline spot — step 7's list of "areas a UVM line move reliably disturbs" (configuration/resource access, the report server's severity counts and message formatting, phasing and objection ownership, sequence/sequencer entry points, factory registration macros) — is generic 1800.2/UVM domain knowledge, not a specific flag, message string, or house convention, so it does not read as a proprietary-lookup violation the way a golden-reference author would flag a specific vendor switch name.
budget_violations: Step 9 allows performance figures to be "read from a file whose path you were given", but the numbered retrieval budget (rules 1-9) allocates Greps/Reads only to the version/marker check (rule 4), three summaries (rule 3), two coverage reports (rule 5), five failure logs (rule 6), and the release-notes/deprecated-symbol sweep (rule 7). The stated total "roughly 24 Greps, 15 Reads and 6 Globs" (line 103) is the exact arithmetic sum of rules 2-7 with nothing left over — verified by adding them up. There is no budgeted call for locating compile time, elaboration time, or peak memory in a build/farm log, even though step 9 explicitly names that as one of two ways the figure could arrive. Contrast with the sibling dv-minimal-reproducer, whose budget explicitly carves out "one Grep of that same log for that line" for its analogous End-of-run summary slot — this skill offers the equivalent lookup in prose without a budget line for it.

Lower confidence: step 6's first classification row routes a build failure on the new release to dv-build-filelist-hygiene "with the quoted first diagnostic," but the skill never Globs or reads the profile's Build log location fact — step 3 Globs only the Regression summary and Coverage output locations, and team-profile.md explicitly distinguishes Build log location from the general Log location as a separate row. If compile/elaboration output lands somewhere other than the per-test regression log this skill does open, quoting that first diagnostic has no budgeted retrieval path in this skill.
review.open_twice: Yes, on balance, but with one section that needs a pass before it earns full trust. The prose voice and density match the golden references closely, the retrieval-budget arithmetic actually adds up exactly (24 Greps / 15 Reads / 6 Globs, verified by summing every numbered rule against every procedure step), the noise-floor discipline in step 4, the per-covergroup coverage re-baselining in step 8, and the Gotchas section are exactly the kind of hard-won, technically correct judgment that makes a skill like this worth reopening. Where it would lose a busy engineer on a second read is the handoff block: a reader filling in `cov model`, `gate`, and the top-level `class`/`phase` fields finds no step telling them how, and will either leave them blank (safe but a nagging gap after all that rigor upstream) or guess — silently reintroducing exactly the two-engineers-disagree problem the rest of the skill is built to prevent. That is a fixable gap in one section (plus the shared review-by date, which is a publishing hygiene issue rather than a content one), not a reason to distrust the method.

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean (single-dir and pack-wide), metadata role/level are exactly dv-infra-engineer/staff, all nine slots are spent, the budget arithmetic is exact (28 Greps / 17 Reads / 6 Globs, matching rule 11), and handoff-vocabulary compliance checks out including the enum-vs-free-text collisions on cov model, gate, proof and axis. But two defects block handing it over. (a) Step 6's tool-semantics row at line 210 says to use "budget rule 9's second Grep over the two build logs' switch lines, side by side", while rule 9 at line 111 scopes that same Grep "against whichever old-side build log path the engineer hands you" and scopes the first Grep to the new side's diagnostic — so the new side's switch lines have no budgeted Grep, and since the two build logs are in different places by the skill's own construction (new side Globbed under the profile's Build log location, old side handed over), one Grep cannot span both. The step cannot be carried out inside the skill's own caps. (b) The handoff field `old fails : <count failing only on the old side, and whether each is fixed or hidden>` (line 332) has no step that assigns the second half: step 5 names the fixed/hidden dichotomy at line 190 but gives no method, and rule 6's five log opens are explicitly directed at the new-only candidates, so nothing is left to decide it — and unlike every other field in this block it offers no honest escape. Also technically wrong on domain: "a covergroup reporting zero bins was never instantiated or never sampled" (lines 281, 397) — never-sampled yields 0 of N, not 0 of 0, since bins total is static; the real producers of a zero total (never instantiated, all bins excluded or made ignore/illegal, an empty binsof/intersect cross) are missed. And the slot-overlap paragraph over-claims at line 72: Performance figures is a strict superset of dv-minimal-reproducer's End-of-run summary (it adds "where compile and elaboration times are recorded"), so "fill it once, reuse the answer" leaves step 9's first two of three numbers unsourced — the exact identity error standing rule 8 polices. I am a fresh reviewer with no baseline, so the new_problems split is my best read of which defects live inside apparatus a fixer would have added (rule 9; the slot-overlap paragraph) rather than a verified diff.
remaining: Line 210 vs line 111: step 6's tool-semantics row demands one Grep 'over the two build logs' switch lines, side by side', but rule 9 budgets its second Grep against the old-side build log only and its first for the new side's diagnostic. No Grep is budgeted for the new side's switch lines, and the two logs are in different directories by construction, so one Grep cannot span them. Either widen rule 9's first Grep pattern to alternate the diagnostic with the switch lines (the device rule 4 already uses for step 2), or budget a third build-log Grep and update rule 11's total.

Line 332: `old fails` asks 'whether each is fixed or hidden' but no step assigns it and no budget funds it — rule 6's five log opens are spent on the new-only candidates per line 195. Either give the field an honest escape ('undetermined' / 'told to you'), or add a bounded method and account for its Greps.

Lines 281 and 397: 'a covergroup reporting zero bins was never instantiated or never sampled' is wrong on the sampling half — an instantiated-but-unsampled covergroup reports its full bins total at zero hits. Replace 'never sampled' with the causes that actually produce a zero total: never instantiated, every bin excluded or turned into ignore/illegal bins, or a binsof/intersect cross that selected nothing.

Line 72: 'Performance figures asks what dv-minimal-reproducer asks under End-of-run summary — fill it once, reuse the answer' claims identity between a slot and its strict superset. This slot adds 'where compile and elaboration times are recorded', which step 9 needs for two of its three numbers. Say how it is wider rather than calling it the same fact.

A zero-bin covergroup is not in step 5's new-only fail set nor among the five opened logs, so the skill's own example has no admissible row. Either widen the block's scope or change the example.
